::: {.callout-note .se-question appearance="simple"}
## The question

[Direction of unit normal vector](https://math.stackexchange.com/questions/1985924/direction-of-unit-normal-vector), asked by [user374859](https://math.stackexchange.com/users/374859/user374859) on Mathematics Stack Exchange (2016-10-26; [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/)):

> Let $S$ be a surface in $\mathbb{R}^3$ given by $z=(x^2+y^2)^{1/2}$ where $x^2+y^2\leq1$. I need to make sure that the normal vector is pointing inwards. I have computed $N$ and found it to be $N=(-z\cos(\theta),-z\sin(\theta),z)$. 
>
> How can I tell if this points inwards or not?
:::

Draw it.  $S$ is a cone with vertex at the origin.  As Parcly mentions in the comments, it has equation $z=r$ in cylindrical coordinates.  The vector $N$ at the point with cylindrical coordinates $(z,\theta,z)$ can be written as $-z \hat{\mathbf{r}} + z \hat{\mathbf{k}}$, where $\hat{\mathbf{r}}$ is the unit vector pointing in the direction of increasing $r$.
